reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about thermodynamic drivers of alloy formation, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook thermodynamics alone does not establish that enthalpy of mixing and surface energy are the decisive competing factors in high-entropy alloy nanoparticle synthesis, nor that composition variation controls this balance in the claimed manner.
premises: Enthalpy of mixing and surface energy are the key competing factors governing alloy formation vs. phase separation in multimetal nanoparticles
The balance between these two factors can be tuned by varying composition
This balance determines whether a homogeneous high-entropy alloy forms with substantial surface-atom exposure
The mechanism applies specifically to systems with more than five interacting noble metal elements
